title: National Grid Reference Map: Plot Any Reference
description: Plot the approximate centre of a British grid reference or click a map to get an approximate grid reference.
summary_sentence: A grid reference names an area; the map shows an approximate centre pin, not its square outline.
quick_answer: Enter a British National Grid reference to plot the approximate centre of its square, or click the map to get an approximate reference. Grid lines and square boundaries are not drawn, and no WGS84–OSGB36 datum shift is applied.
steps_intro: A reference is an address. See where it lives:

body.t: Plot the approximate centre of a guidebook reference for orientation. Confirm important locations with an authoritative conversion and mapping source.
A centre pin is not a square boundary or a verified planning boundary; use official plans for site decisions.
A reference’s precision describes its square size. This map does not draw the grid or square outlines.
The workspace plots one reference at a time, not a distribution map. Verify coordinates before using them in records.

examples.label: Example · The square is the statement

body.t: A six-figure grid reference identifies a 100 m square. This workspace plots its approximate centre, not the square outline.
Map context may help spot an input error, but a pin cannot prove a reference is correct. The conversion also omits the datum shift.

popular_table.title: Grid-reference precision
popular_table.intro: A reference identifies a square at the stated precision; this map plots an approximate centre pin only.
popular_table.note: Only an approximate centre pin is drawn; there are no grid lines or square outlines.

faq: Why does the map draw a square instead of a pin?
It does not draw the grid square. It places a pin at the approximate centre of an entered reference; the reference represents an area.
Can I plot several references at once?
The workspace plots one reference centre at a time.
What if my reference has spaces?
Spaces in supported grid references are ignored, for example TQ 292 796 and TQ292796.
The square landed in the sea.
The map plots a centre pin, not a square. Check the reference and use an authoritative datum transformation before relying on its position.
Does the map show OS mapping itself?
It uses the site’s web map, not OS map sheets, and does not display grid lines or square outlines.
How do I read a reference off the map?
Click a point to get six- and ten-figure approximate references. The tool does not apply the WGS84–OSGB36 datum shift.
